title: Ordinary flat exchange for a prescribed vertical adjunction
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and $g:S\to Y$ flat [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism], with $Z=X\times_Y S$ and projections $q:Z\to X$, $p:Z\to S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix an adjunction $a:f^*\dashv f_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Use the chosen tensor-pullback adjunctions for $g,q,p$, and write $a_R$ for the chosen $p$-adjunction. Let $\alpha:q_*f_*\simeq p_*g_*$ be the composite of pushforwardComp$(q,f)$, pushforwardCongr$(qf=pg)$, and inverse pushforwardComp$(p,g)$. Let $c:g^*p^*\simeq f^*q^*$ be the inverse conjugate of $\alpha$ under $a$ composed with the $q$-adjunction and the $g$-adjunction composed with $a_R$ [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. Let $B:f_*\circ g^*\to q^*\circ p_*$ (composition in diagrammatic order) be the natural transformation whose component at $M$ is moduleBaseChangeMap$(f,p,g,q,qf=pg,M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction]. Then $B_M$ is invertible whenever $M$ is quasi-coherent, and for every $\mathcal O_Y$-module $N$, $g^*(\eta^a_N)\,B_{f^*N}=\eta^{a_R}_{g^*N}\,p_*(c_N)$, where products of arrows are written in diagrammatic order. The adjunction, natural transformation and composition isomorphism in this statement are the displayed fixed formulas.

source.place: Part (1), degree zero; Tag 02N7, resolution construction and augmentation diagram; Tag 0B65, conjugation of adjunctions

proof.text: Use the explicitly chosen adjunctions and the sectionwise pushforward comparison α. Conjugating α under the two composite adjunctions gives the explicitly specified c. The ordinary exchange B is the adjoint of f_* of the q-unit followed by α. Naturality of the q-unit and the pushforward comparison, followed by naturality of the g Hom equivalence, proves naturality of B on all modules.

The conjugate unit equation says that the composite f,q unit followed by α equals the composite g,p unit followed by p_*g_* of c. Expand the composite units. Take the g-adjoint of g*η^a_N followed by B_(f*N); naturality of the g-unit moves η^a_N before the g-unit at f_*f*N. The defining adjoint equation for B identifies the remaining composite with f_* of the q-unit followed by α. Apply the preceding conjugate unit equation. This is the g-adjoint of the claimed right side, so injectivity of the Hom equivalence proves the unit identity.

Compare B with the resolution comparison in degree zero. Choose resolutions and an augmented lift as in the base-change section theorem. The canonical zeroth-derived-functor identifications send the two augmentations to the identity on the ordinary modules; the augmentation equation identifies the degree-zero adjoint with f_* of the q-unit followed by α. Therefore, after exchanging the two fibre-product models by symmetry, the degree-zero resolution beta is B. Proper f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and q is flat as a base change of g. The resolution comparison is invertible on each quasi-coherent M by flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta_isIso; transport through the zeroth-derived identifications and symmetry proves invertibility of B_M. No injectivity of completion or nonempty scheme is used.

proof_origin.place: Degree-zero specialization of part (1); 02N7 augmented resolution diagram, with 0B65 for the explicit adjunction conjugate

lean.statement:
theorem ordinary_flat_exchange_prescribed_adjunction
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (g : S ⟶ Y) [Flat g]
    (adj : Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f ⊣ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f) :
    let p := pullback.snd f g
    let q := pullback.fst f g
    let adjR := Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction p)
    let c := (conjugateIsoEquiv
      (adj.comp (Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction q)))
      ((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction g)).comp adjR)).symm
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp q f ≪≫
          Scheme.Modules.pushforwardCongr pullback.condition ≪≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp p g).symm)
    let B : Scheme.Modules.pushforward f ⋙ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g ⟶
        Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback q ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward p :=
      { app := fun M ↦ Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChangeMap f p g q pullback.condition M
        naturality := fun _ _ a ↦
          Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChangeMap_naturality f p g q pullback.condition a }
    (∀ (M : X.Modules), M.IsQuasicoherent → IsIso (B.app M)) ∧
      (∀ (N : Y.Modules),
        (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).map (adj.unit.app N) ≫
          B.app ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).obj N) =
        adjR.unit.app ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj N) ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pushforward p).map (c.hom.app N))
